title: Automatic generation of model sequences for complex regions in assembly graphs with TTT.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Zenodo record 20836977 API: one file, TTT-0.1.1.zip (2.5 MB), which is the algorithm source code and not a dataset. Listed the GenomeArk S3 prefix for zebra finch chrZ: assembled FASTA files of about 94-97 MB each, so over the 50 MB cap and not downloaded. Europe PMC supplementary file listing timed out.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: Data availability statement: HG002 reads are on the HPRC (Human Pangenome Reference Consortium) S3 bucket, giraffe reads under BioProject PRJNA1367195, and zebra finch raw reads under PRJNA1241433. Any number of tangles evaluated would come from the paper, but I did not count them.

a1_downloadable.note: Code (Zenodo) and assembly FASTA (GenomeArk S3) are public with no login. Checked the listings only.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: No labelled table exists. The paper is a graph-traversal algorithm, and a 'correct tangle resolution' label would have to be built by running assemblers and comparing against T2T (telomere-to-telomere) references.

a3_inputs_present.note: The inputs are raw long-read sequencing data and assembly graphs, which would have to be regenerated from SRA or S3 reads.

a4_units_stated.note: There are no tabular measurements to carry units.

a5_enough_rows.note: Only a handful of genomes (human HG002, giraffe, zebra finch). The number of tangles is not verified and is likely small.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: Tens to hundreds of GB of raw reads per genome
a6_fits_laptop.note: Rebuilding assembly graphs needs HPC (high-performance computing) resources. The paper itself used the NIH Biowulf cluster.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Not checkable, because there is no table to count.

a8_label_provenance.note: Any truth label would itself be an assembly output (a curated or other assembler's T2T sequence), not a direct measurement.

honest_claim_h3: No ML claim is possible. The deliverable is an assembly algorithm benchmarked on three genomes, not a labelled dataset.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use read coverage and alignment features of tangled genome-assembly regions to predict the correct path through each tangle.
plain_idea.train_on: Tangles in assembly graphs (knots of near-identical repeats where the assembler cannot decide the order). The number of examples is unknown and likely tiny across three genomes.
plain_idea.predict: The correct traversal (ordering and copy number) of each tangle. The truth comes from curated T2T assemblies, which are themselves computational products.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Genome assembly teams could replace manual curation of gaps. But there is no labelled data here, and building it needs HPC-scale reassembly.

ml_idea: Learn tangle resolution from assembly-graph features. This is infeasible here: there is no label table, the inputs are raw reads, and the compute is HPC-scale.

effort.compute_note: Not estimated, because the project fails Part A. Regenerating assembly graphs from raw reads is cluster-scale work.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Look for any released per-tangle table (features plus correct traversal). There is none: Zenodo holds only the code zip.

verdict_reason: Algorithm paper with no labelled table (A2 fails). The only inputs are raw reads and assembly FASTA needing HPC (A3, A5, A6 fail), and any truth label would itself be an assembly output (A8).
